# FwaConversionFloor

<!-- generated by scripts/render.mjs from data/ ; do not edit -->

Minimum-output policy for every FWAT buy the Midway engine drives (accrued-reward claims, managed FWAT settlement). Registered on MidwayRegistry as `conversionFloor` and replaceable by the registry operator; the engine reads it at call time. The effective floor for a buy of `ethIn` is the strictest of four legs: - observation: expected output at the best (highest FWAT per ETH) pool price among the recorded observations that are usable, after the 1% hook fee, less `slippageCapBps`. An observation is usable when it was recorded in an earlier block and is at most `observationWindowBlocks` old. Fewer than `minObservations` usable observations make the floor invalid and the engine refuses the buy; - spot: the same quote at the pool's current `sqrtPriceX96`, less `slippageCapBps`; - FWA: FWAToken's own `buybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` when armed (the min-sqrt sentinel and any invalid read count as no FWA floor); - absolute: `floorRate` FWAT per ETH when nonzero. The result must clear `MIN_FLOOR_RATE` on `ethIn` or it is invalid. The pool exposes no oracle. `recordObservation` is permissionless and stores the live spot in the ring slot of the current bucket (`observationWindowBlocks / OBSERVATION_SLOTS` blocks per bucket); within a bucket the highest FWAT per ETH price is kept, so a recorded observation is replaced only by a stricter one and ages out with its bucket. A pushed price reaches the floor only when every usable observation is at a pushed price, which needs the pool held at that price across `minObservations` buckets: from `bucketBlocks * (minObservations - 2) + 2` blocks when the ring is empty (18 at launch) up to the whole window when honest observations are present. Sells through the pool are open to every FWAT holder, so a held push is exposed to holders selling into it; the holder set is small because FWAT is otherwise transfer locked. The cost is one round trip of the hook fee on the pushed amount plus that capital held, so the floor removes the same-block sandwich, not a held one. An observation recorded at a price above the current one makes the floor stricter than the pool can pay until its bucket ages out of the window.

**Address**: [`0x53A4B5954a577a100780512885f78581D9F9F41C`](https://evm.now/address/0x53A4B5954a577a100780512885f78581D9F9F41C?chainId=1)

## Functions

### State changing

| Function | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| `recordObservation()` | Store the pool's current `sqrtPriceX96` as the observation of the current bucket. Anyone may call. When the bucket already holds an observation, the call succeeds only with a higher FWAT per ETH price; otherwise it reverts `ObservationNotImproved`. Reverts when the pool cannot be read. The observation becomes usable in the next block. |
| `setFloorRate(uint256)` | Set the absolute floor. Zero disables it; any other value must be at least `MIN_FLOOR_RATE`. |
| `setMinObservations(uint8)` | Set the usable observations required for a valid floor. Zero disables the observation leg; any other value is at most `OBSERVATION_SLOTS`. |
| `setObservationWindowBlocks(uint32)` | Set the observation window. At least `OBSERVATION_SLOTS` and at most `MAX_OBSERVATION_WINDOW_BLOCKS`. Bucket boundaries move with the window: stored observations keep their block, age out on the new window, and a stored observation whose block no longer maps to the current bucket of its slot is replaced by the next record in that slot at any price. |
| `setSlippageCapBps(uint16)` | Set the slippage cap. At most `MAX_SLIPPAGE_CAP_BPS`. |

### View

| Function | Notice |
| --- | --- |
| `currentBucketObservation()` | The observation stored for the current bucket, if any. `recorded` is false when the bucket's ring slot is empty or holds an observation from an earlier bucket. |
| `floorId()` |  |
| `floorRate()` | Optional absolute floor in FWAT per ETH scaled by 1e18. Zero disables it. |
| `fwaToken()` |  |
| `MAX_OBSERVATION_WINDOW_BLOCKS()` | Upper bound on `observationWindowBlocks` (about one day). |
| `MAX_SLIPPAGE_CAP_BPS()` | Upper bound on `slippageCapBps`: a spot-relative leg never sits more than 10% under its reference price. |
| `MIN_FLOOR_RATE()` | Lowest nonzero `floorRate` accepted, and the dust bound every effective floor must clear: 1e15 = 0.001 FWAT per ETH. A weaker bound reads as configured while permitting a buy at effectively any output. |
| `MIN_SQRT_PRICE_SENTINEL()` | Uniswap v3 MIN_SQRT_PRICE + 1. FWAToken carries this as `buybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` when its buyback has no price limit; it derives a zero output floor at any realistic scale, so it is read as no FWA floor rather than a floor of zero. |
| `minimumOutput(uint256)` | The effective minimum output for a buy of `ethIn`. `valid` is false when fewer than `minObservations` observations are usable, when no leg exists, or when the combined floor is below `MIN_FLOOR_RATE` on `ethIn`. `fwaSqrtPriceLimitX96` is FWAToken's raw limit when it is a usable floor, else zero. |
| `minObservations()` | Usable observations required for a valid floor. Zero disables the observation leg. |
| `OBSERVATION_SLOTS()` | Observation ring size, and the upper bound on `minObservations`. |
| `observationAt(uint256)` | The stored observation at ring index `index` (0 to `OBSERVATION_SLOTS` - 1). |
| `observationWindowBlocks()` | Age in blocks past which an observation is not usable. At least `OBSERVATION_SLOTS` so every ring slot maps to a bucket of at least one block. |
| `registry()` |  |
| `slippageCapBps()` | Slippage cap in bps applied to the observation and spot legs. Zero disables the spot leg and makes the observation leg exact. |
| `spotQuote(uint256)` | The pool's current `sqrtPriceX96` and the expected FWAT output for `ethIn` at that price after the 1% hook fee, before the slippage cap. `valid` is false when the PoolManager read fails or the pool is uninitialized. |
| `usableObservations()` | The usable observations right now and the best (highest FWAT per ETH) `sqrtPriceX96` among them. `bestSqrtPriceX96` is zero when none is usable. |
